newsitem.title: THAILAND: Italian Thai rules out withdrawal from Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Italian Thai rules out withdrawal from Philippines.

text.p: Italian-Thai Development Plc said on Friday it would complete its Philippine land reclamation project despite allegations over the contract.
"We're in for the duration, that's pretty certain. We've probably invested far too much to pull out now," said Trevor Bird, Italian-Thai's project development manager.

Italian-Thai, one of Thailand's largest construction contractors, is a shareholder of the Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp which has been contracted to reclaim and develop 750 square hectares of land in the Manila Bay area.
Philippine Senate President Ernesto Maceda said last year Amari had bought the land from state-run Public Estates Authority at an unusually big discount to the market price.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos has since December ordered a review of all contracts related to the 1,500-hectare (3,700 acre) Manila Bay development programme.
Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc, owning about 40 percent of Centennial City, the main partner in the Amari project, has also pledged not to pull out of the project.
The Philippines is a major business target for Italian-Thai which seeks to secure contracts to redevelop part of the Clark airforce base and on other hydro-electric projects, Bird said.
